answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds tie each validator's stake to a zero-knowledge verifiable delay, forcing any Sybil replica to lock collateral exceeding the discounted reward. A subgame-perfect slashing matrix then imposes a penalty quadratic in the multiplied weight, yielding a strictly negative expected utility for identity multiplication. The resulting Nash equilibrium is robust because no coalition can profit without revealing the pearl of its hidden state across the tundra of adversarial strategies at the vertex of the game tree.
